## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading as a configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. In this mode, an application’s runtime configuration interacts with the extensions it imports.

If an extension does not explicitly declare support for free threading, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The way an extension makes this declaration depends on whether it uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

The declaration signals that the extension supports the runtime mode; it does not establish that the extension’s code is thread-safe. Extension authors have a separate responsibility to make their code safe for use with free threading.
